title: Multicompartmental analysis of the microbiome in the context of liver transplants
summary:
After liver transplantation, complications may occur, but their causes are not fully understood. Recent findings show that bacteria are present not only in the intestine but also in bile and may influence recovery after surgery.

In this study, we investigate how these microorganisms change before, during, and after transplantation. Blood, stool, bile and small tissue samples will be collected at defined time points up to one year after surgery. The aim is to better understand the relationship between the microbiome, the immune system and graft function, and to enable new treatment strategies in the future.
conditions: Liver transplantation in end-stage liver disease (particularly metabolic/nutritional cirrhosis)

interventions.name: Participants undergo guideline-based liver transplantation without any study-related therapeutic intervention. Prospective sample collection only (blood, stool, bile and liver tissue) is performed preoperatively, intraoperatively and at predefined postoperative time points up to 12 months after tran

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•    Listed for elective liver transplantation at the participating centre.
•    Clinically stable at the time of informed consent.
•    Willingness and ability to provide preoperative stool samples and attend the specified follow-up appointments (up to 12 months).
•    Familiarity with the study requirements or sufficient language skills to understand the consent form and instructions.
Exclusion criteria:
• High-urgency or emergency transplantation (not a planned elective procedure), as preoperative samples and standardised information cannot be guaranteed.
• Inability to give informed consent (e.g. lack of cognitive ability, lack of language skills without an interpreter), or unwillingness to participate/follow up.
• Transplantation in combination with other organs (e.g. liver-kidney) or planned simultaneous major procedures if this significantly alters post-operative care and sample collection.
